 Darius Acuff Jr., Zach LaVine, De’Andre Hunter, Precious Achiuwa and Dylan Cardwell will start Sunday’s game against the Heat. 
 The Kings are without Domantas Sabonis (knee) for Sunday’s game, opening up a spot in the starting lineup. Cardwell will replace him, and the Kings will need his rebounding and defense. Also, Hunter reclaims his place in the lineup with Leaky Black heading to the bench. And Achiuwa remains in the starting lineup despite Keegan Murray returning from an ankle injury. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Domantas Sabonis (knee) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Heat. 
 Sabonis is a late addition to the Kings’ injury report due to a sore left knee. If he can’t play against the Heat, the Kings will have to rely more on Dylan Cardwell in the post. 
 Keegan Murray

 Keegan Murray (ankle) is available for Sunday’s game against the Heat. 
 Sunday’s game will be Murray’s first since October 23. It’s unclear whether his playing time will be limited, but fantasy managers shouldn’t expect to see Murray’s minutes go well into the thirties. Precious Achiuwa has been the starting power forward in Murray’s absence.

 De’Andre Hunter (illness) is not on the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Heat. 
 Hunter did not play in Friday’s loss to the Spurs, with Leaky Black replacing him in the starting lineup. Black has played significant minutes recently due to his defensive ability, and that should remain the case on Sunday.

 The Sacramento Kings will start Darius Acuff, Zach LaVine, Leaky Black, Precious Achiuwa, and Domantas Sabonis on Friday. 
 DeAndre Hunter (illness) will not play against the Spurs on Friday, so Leaky Black will get the start. Leaky has been an energy guy who has gained some favor in the eyes of Doug Christie. If you’re in a deeper league, Leaky Black could be worth a stream, but the ball won’t be in his hands with this current iteration of the Kings.

 Paul George amassed a team-high 27 points (11-of-18 FGs), three rebounds, one assist and two steals over 28 minutes to lead the Celtics to a 117-97 win over the Bucks on Sunday.
 Here’s an oversimplification: George has fit seamlessly into Boston’s existing nucleus early on this season. He knocked down several difficult shots, including 4-of-6 from three-point range, on his way to a 20-point first half against a rebuilding Milwaukee squad. He posted 16 points in the second quarter alone. The 36-year-old veteran would’ve put together another monster scoring effort, but he was barely needed in the second half as Boston’s extremely deep bench took care of business. The Celtics have a three-game week on tap featuring matchups against the 76ers, Raptors and Mavericks. All eyes will be on the Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum showdown, but George will be taking on his former team for the first time in Philadelphia on Tuesday night.
 -  George Bissell

 Kyle Kuzma 
 MIL 
 Forward

 Player Stats

 Kyle Kuzma accumulated a team-high 27 points (10-of-17 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, one assist and two blocks over 31 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.
 Kuzma came out firing away and never really slowed down, hoisting a team-high 17 shot attempts in this one. He carried Milwaukee offensively in the opening half, scoring 21 points on 8-of-14 shooting, but the Bucks managed just 45 points overall. It certainly didn’t help matters that Tyler Herro left the game with an apparent left knee injury midway through the third quarter. He’ll continue to have the green light from the moment he steps on the floor, but he doesn’t offer enough fantasy appeal to be worthy of a roster spot in shallow mixed leagues. The free-falling Bucks have lost six straight games and are 1-9 overall this season. They have a four-game week coming up that includes matchups against the Knicks, Lakers, Magic and Hawks.
 -  George Bissell

 Jayson Tatum tallied 21 points (6-of-19 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, one steal and one block over 29 minutes in Sunday’s win over the Bucks.
 Tatum got off to a sizzling-hot start, shredding a lackluster Milwaukee squad for 16 first-quarter points. He was able to shift into cruise control as Boston built a 13-point halftime advantage. It wasn’t a particularly efficient shooting performance as he went just 1-of-8 from inside the arc, but knocked down 5-of-11 from long range. He wasn’t really needed in the second half as Boston’s extremely deep bench was able to take care of business against a struggling Milwaukee squad that lost Tyler Herro midway through the third quarter. The Celtics have a three-game week on tap featuring matchups against the 76ers, Raptors and Mavericks. All eyes will be on the highly-anticipated Tatum and Jaylen Brown matchup on Tuesday night.
 -  George Bissell

 Brayden Burries recorded 13 points (5-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, four assists and one block over 29 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.
 Burries has been one of the few bright spots for the rebuilding Bucks this season and is starting to make some noise from a fantasy perspective. He followed up a career-high 21-point performance against the Raptors on Friday with another double-digit scoring effort while also pulling down eight boards as well. Burries is worth a speculative add in deeper fantasy leagues, particularly with the rebuilding Bucks seemingly willing to give him an extended opportunity to develop.
 -  George Bissell

 Mitchell Robinson delivered 12 points (6-of-6 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, four steals and one block over 18 minutes off the bench in Sunday’s win over the Bucks.
 It was encouraging to see Robinson deliver an impactful performance on both ends of the floor off the bench after entering the contest questionable due to illness. The 28-year-old big man continues to take a back seat to Neemias Queta, who had 13 points and nine rebounds in 22 minutes in this one, but it hasn’t prevented him from remaining a force on the glass.
 -  George Bissell

 Day’Ron Sharpe produced six points (2-of-5 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, two steals and two blocks in Sunday’s loss to the Mavericks.
 The good news is that Sharpe provided solid defensive contributions and assists on Sunday. However, the lackluster scoring production continues, with the center failing to crack double figures in points for the seventh time in 10 games. Sharpe’s role as Brooklyn’s starting center makes him challenging to move on from in 12-team leagues. However, he may be a “buy low” candidate for managers willing to overlook the lack of scoring. But don’t look to acquire Sharpe this week, as the Nets only play two games in Week 4.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Nolan Traoré accounted for 14 points (6-of-15 FGs), one rebound, two assists and two three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Mavericks.
 While he didn’t add much value in the assist column, Traoré extended his streak of double-digit scoring to five games. After a disappointing rookie season, the second-year guard has started the Nets’ last seven games and appears unlikely to give up that spot anytime soon. Traoré is rostered in 42 percent of Yahoo leagues, which is a fair number at this point in the season.

 Julius Randle tallied 13 points (5-of-10 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, four assists and one block in Sunday’s loss to the Mavericks.
 Randle’s ten field-goal attempts and 13 points were the second-fewest he’s recorded in a game in those categories this season. His assist production was decent, but those rostering Randle likely hoped for more in the final game of the week. More troubling for fantasy managers is the Nets’ upcoming schedule, as they’re one of two teams that play just two games next week.

 Michael Porter Jr. recorded 19 points (5-of-15 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), nine rebounds, one steal and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Mavericks.
 Eleven of Porter’s 15 shot attempts came from beyond the arc on Sunday, and a 1-of-4 night from two helped lower his overall field-goal percentage. MPJ has scored at least 20 points in six of his 10 games, and he’s made multiple three-pointers in nine of 10 games. Even with Sunday’s low field-goal percentage, Porter is still providing top-50 fantasy value, exceeding his preseason ADP. The bad news for fantasy managers is that the Nets play two games next week, starting with the Pelicans on Wednesday.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Santi Aldama amassed 12 points (5-of-7 FGs), two rebounds, one steal and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Nets.
 Making his second appearance for the Mavericks, Aldama played 15 minutes and scored in double figures for the first time in a Mavericks uniform. His ability to step away from the basket and hit shots gives the Mavericks a dimension their other bigs don’t bring. Getting the minutes needed to provide consistent fantasy value may be a challenge because of Dallas’ frontcourt depth, but Aldama should be a fixture in the rotation.
